references.text: Aaron and his sons shall keep the lamps burning from evening to morning before the Lord, a parallel to burning incense at twilight.
The preceding verse describing the morning incense when the lamps are tended, together with the evening incense, makes up the daily incense offering service.
The continual burnt offering before the Lord throughout all generations, using the same terminology for the 'tamid' (continual) service.
The continual burnt offering instituted on Mount Sinai, part of the daily worship service along with the incense.
Aaron shall tend the lamps continually before the Lord, connected to the lamp service performed together with the incense offering.
Prayer is compared to incense before God's face, and lifted hands to the evening sacrifice.
The incense rises before God's face along with the prayers of the saints, fulfilling the continual incense offering in heaven.
Zechariah burns incense in the temple while the people pray outside, showing the continuation of the incense service during the time of the second temple.
The priests burn incense before the Lord every morning and evening, continuing the regular incense service.
The lamps shall be set up so that they shine forward, part of the holy service performed together with the incense.
Complementary instructions about the eternal night service: Incense and light are to be maintained continually before the Lord's face.
Complementary instructions about the perpetual light that illuminates the context of the incense ritual.
